Done. Summary of the T3 solution (condition F, free tooling choice):

- **Approach**: a plain Python script (`out/T3/solution.py`) built on `safetensors` + `torch` directly, rather than `transformers.save_pretrained(torch_dtype=...)` — that API applies one dtype to the whole model with no per-tensor-name override, which can't express "112 of 114 tensors go to bf16, 2 stay fp32."
- **Casting**: a tight regex (`model.layers.<i>.(self_attn.{q,k,v,o}_proj|mlp.{gate,up,down}_proj).weight`) matches exactly the 112 projection matrices — deliberately not a broad `.*weight` pattern, since that would also catch `embed_tokens`/`lm_head`.
- **Required checks** run and raise `AssertionError` before any file is written: exactly 112 bf16 tensors, `q_proj` layer 0 is bf16, `embed_tokens.weight` is fp32, total tensor count is 114.
- **Sharding**: greedy bin-packing capped at 268,435,456 bytes of tensor data per shard, with an explicit oversized-tensor branch so `embed_tokens.weight` and `lm_head.weight` (412 MB each, over the cap) each get their own shard, matching the spec.
- **Result**: ran once, succeeded — `out/T3/` has 10 shards + `model.safetensors.index.json`, verified independently (114 tensors total, 112 bf16, embed/lm_head fp32, all shards ≤256 MiB of tensor data).
- Wrote `out/T3/run.sh` (invokes the script from repo root) and `out/T3/REPORT.md` with the self-report.
